name: Ifrane
hero_subtitle: Morocco’s alpine town in the Middle Atlas — cedars, lakes, cool air and the stone lion.

info.entry_val: Road from Fes (~1 h) or Meknes (~1 h)

overview.title: Alpine air in the Middle Atlas
overview.p1: Ifrane sits above 1,600 m in the Middle Atlas, built in the 1930s with pitched roofs and European-style chalets. Locals call it the Little Switzerland of Morocco: cool summers, possible snow in winter, cedar forests and a string of mountain lakes nearby. It is a short drive from Fes or Meknes and a natural base for Dayet Aoua, the Ifrane National Park and Michlifen.
overview.p2: One full day covers the town, the stone lion, a lake and a walk under the cedars. Stay longer for hiking, skiing in season at Michlifen, or a quieter pace than the imperial cities. Expect mountain weather — pack a layer even in summer.

detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Dayet Aoua — walk the shore and watch for birds.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Dinner in town; mountain nights can be chilly.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Cedar forest trails and the Gouraud cedar area.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Michlifen viewpoint or a quiet stop at Dayet Hachlaf.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return to Ifrane for a relaxed meal.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Source Tizguit or Source Vittel and a short nature walk.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Ifrane National Park edge or campus viewpoints at Al Akhawayn.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last mint tea before the road back to Fes or Meknes.

food.title: Eating in the mountains
food.p1: Ifrane’s food scene is simpler than Fes or Marrakech: hotel restaurants, cafés and grills. Fresh air and walking build an appetite; plan a proper meal in town after lake or forest outings.
food.li2: Centre cafés for breakfast and coffee.
food.li3: Bring water and snacks for lake and forest trips.
food.li4: Mountain evenings can be cold — indoor seating helps.
food.li5: Limited options at remote viewpoints — eat before you go.

1.title: Altitude & weather
1.desc: Above 1,600 m — nights are cool year-round; snow is possible in winter. Pack layers.

2.title: Getting around
2.desc: A car is ideal for lakes, cedars and Michlifen. Grand taxis from Fes or Meknes reach the town.

3.title: Nature respect
3.desc: Stay on paths in the national park and cedar areas; do not disturb wildlife or carve trees.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Ifrane
daytrips.subtitle: Lakes, forests and routes toward Azrou and the wider Middle Atlas.

azrou.title: Azrou
azrou.desc: Cedar market town about 30 minutes south — forest roads and often macaques nearby.

fes.title: Fes
fes.desc: About 1 hour by road — imperial medina if you combine mountain and city.

meknes.title: Meknes
meknes.desc: About 1 hour by road — another imperial city on the way to or from Ifrane.

timahdite.title: Timahdite area
timahdite.desc: High plateau and rural Middle Atlas landscapes south of Ifrane.

q1.question: How many days in Ifrane?
q1.answer: One full day covers the highlights; two or three suit hiking, lakes and a slower mountain pace.

q2.question: Is Ifrane cold?
q2.answer: Cooler than the plains year-round. Summers are pleasant; winters can bring snow and freezing nights.

q3.question: Do I need a car?
q3.answer: Strongly recommended for Dayet Aoua, the cedars and Michlifen. The town centre is walkable.

q4.question: Can I ski?
q4.answer: Michlifen offers limited ski facilities in season (roughly December–March); conditions vary year to year.

q5.question: Far from Fes?
q5.answer: About one hour by road — an easy day trip or overnight from Fes or Meknes.
